name: Religious democracy
summary: Religious democracy is a system in which government is chosen and held accountable by popular vote while a religion's values and law set the framework for legislation and public life. In its main modern form, Islamic, God holds ultimate sovereignty and the people exercise a divinely granted right to choose their rulers and run public affairs, with jurists or a religious council checking laws against sharia.
scope: The profile represents the official Iranian-Islamic formulation, the Islamic Republic's constitution and Ayatollah Khamenei's theory of mardomsalari-ye dini, which the typical adherent follows, while noting the Maududi 'theo-democracy' and Soroush's reformist variant as strands. It excludes Christian democracy as a party family (see christian-democracy), secular democracy, and pure clerical theocracy.

keyFigures.name: Ali Khamenei
keyFigures.role: Iran's Supreme Leader, who made 'religious democracy' an official theory of the state.

keyFigures.name: Abdolkarim Soroush
keyFigures.role: Iranian philosopher who defined religious democracy as religious values in the public life of a religious society, within justice and human rights.

keyFigures.name: Abul A'la Maududi
keyFigures.role: Proposed a 'theo-democracy' of pious Muslims under divine law.

sources.usedFor: The religious and democratic elements of the official Iranian theory: sovereignty of religion, legitimacy of the people's vote, people as masters of public affairs.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The constitution reserves major industries to the state and plans development; adherents accept private trade but not market primacy.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 44 places large industries, banking, energy, transport and communications in the state sector.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Islamic almsgiving and khums fund the poor, but sources on religious democracy do not address progressive taxation; adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 47 protects only legitimately acquired property and Article 49 mandates confiscation of illicit wealth, so property can be overridden.

worker-ownership.rationale: Article 44 gives the cooperative sector a place beside state and private, but collective workplace ownership is not a central demand.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug use is prohibited as forbidden under Islamic criteria that all laws must follow (Art. 4).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents restrict speech harmful to Islam but the statement concerns group-hatred law; practice and rationale are mixed.

strong-leader.rationale: The theory stresses people as masters of public affairs and independent branches, though a supervising jurist leader exists; unchecked bypassing is not endorsed.

state-harmful.rationale: The theory is about building a state grounded in religion; the constitution creates strong state institutions under Islamic law.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Prostitution is forbidden under Islamic criteria that must ground all laws (Art. 4).

decide-locally.rationale: The constitution provides elected local councils (Art. 100) within a unitary state; adherents are not indifferent but not strong either.

traditional-family.rationale: Article 10 makes the family the fundamental unit of society and requires laws to strengthen it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Same-sex relations conflict with Islamic law that must ground legislation under Article 4.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious democracy is defined as a democracy that builds a religion's values into government, so a larger public role is central.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Article 20 frames equality as in conformity with Islamic criteria, implying fixed gender roles from religion.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The constitution centers Islamic culture and Persian language and aims to preserve cultural heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Reformers like Soroush favor gradual reform while others stress revolutionary foundations; adherents are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Article 152 rejects domination and hegemonic powers; adherents distrust Western-led international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Constitution favors planned development and self-sufficiency, and rejects economic domination by foreign powers.

nation-first.rationale: Art. 152 and 153 prioritize independence and forbid foreign domination, though Islamic solidarity also matters.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Art. 154 supports oppressed peoples but forbids interference in other nations' internal affairs.

limit-growth.rationale: Constitution aims at economic growth and self-sufficiency; limiting growth is not a position of the theory.

central-planning.rationale: Article 44 sets planned development with three sectors, not full central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Article 44's cooperative and state sectors alongside markets fit this mixed view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Islamic inheritance law fixes shares for heirs, so heavy taxation of inheritances conflicts with it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Self-sufficiency and independence from foreign economic domination favor protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Art. 44 requires planned development with strategic sectors in state hands.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The constitution protects private income from lawful work (Art. 46) and wage labor within Islamic norms.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Banking is nationalized in Article 44, with a state central bank assumed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 26 permits parties within Islamic limits and Article 6 requires elections, so single-party rule is not the model.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The system is a republic that replaced a monarchy and the constitution rejects hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents claim democracy grounded in religion but not best "even when voters choose badly" unconditionally, since religion sets limits.

direct-votes.rationale: Article 59 allows referenda on major issues, but this is not a central demand.

workers-councils.rationale: The constitution relies on parliament and elected councils, not workers' councils as basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The constitution proclaims territorial integrity and national unity as inviolable.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule by qualified jurists (Art. 107-109) assumes some are better suited, though framed as qualification.

political-violence-never.rationale: The theory emerged from revolution and permits defense; adherents do not hold political violence is never justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religious democracy gives religion a place in government; secular separation is the criticism it rejects.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Article 4 requires all civil, penal and other laws to rest on Islamic criteria.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Judiciary and army are state organs under the constitution; privatization of justice and defense is unthinkable.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Article 19 gives equal rights to all peoples of Iran; religion, not ethnicity, defines the community.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The theory views history through faith and justice; Islamic republicans reject Marxist class conflict as the driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Islamic justice stresses fairness and removal of deprivation but not equality of outcomes.

civilizational-union.rationale: The preamble calls for the unity of the Islamic ummah and Article 11 directs government to work toward it.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Religious ethics stress duty and the common good over self-interest as a moral basis.

limit-population.rationale: Iran has swung between limiting and promoting births; religious conservatives favor family growth, so active limiting is not an adherent position.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The constitution aims at industrial development and self-sufficiency, not rejection of industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Adherents want scientific progress but within Islamic criteria and institutions; no stated position on disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The theory claims return to Islamic values while embracing modern institutions; split on restoration versus progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents ground policy in religious principle and criteria, not purely results.

direct-action.rationale: The theory channels the people's role through elections and institutions.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No religious-democratic strand advocates this; the state promotes development.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Constitution protects occupations and wage work; abolition is a Marxist idea.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Islamic justice prizes meeting basic needs, but reward by work is protected in Article 46.

production-for-use.rationale: Article 43 aims at meeting needs, yet private profit is allowed; split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Article 46 protects income from lawful work and Article 47 legitimate ownership, rejecting the Marxist claim.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule rests on Islamic law and elections, not class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Constitution protects private and cooperative farming; compulsory collectivization not endorsed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialism is strong but a Marxist theory of inevitable capitalist war is not the doctrine.

taxation-theft.rationale: Islamic zakat and khums are religious obligations and the state taxes under law; the claim conflicts with that.

harm-principle.rationale: Religious democracy restricts conduct on religious criteria beyond preventing harm to others, as the legalist and critic sources note.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are framed within Islamic criteria and community; Article 13 gives recognized minorities group standing.

conscription.rationale: Article 151 and the system's military organization accept compulsory service; defense is a duty.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The theory stresses people's right to vote as central to legitimacy.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a vehicle for religious and social aims, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Articles 3 and 43 commit the state to providing material means and eliminating deprivation.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Islamic universalism rejects racial hierarchy; Art. 19 and 20 affirm equal rights regardless of race.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation is through elected parliament by direct secret ballot (Art. 62), plus councils.

total-state.rationale: The constitution protects private ownership and spheres of citizen life, though under Islamic criteria.

national-rebirth.rationale: The revolution is framed as renewal; not clearly a doctrine of radical rebirth after decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Article 152 and 154 reject domination and interference; the theory is not expansionist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule rests on constitution and elections, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Article 23 and the guarantees of free choice of occupation (Art. 28) exclude binding labor to land.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Soroush sees religious knowledge as fallible human understanding, but others hold revealed truth; mostly rejects the claim.

universal-morality.rationale: Religion supplies universal moral truths; the legalist view holds a rigid reading of sacred texts.

single-common-good.rationale: Islamic justice and the common good are held to guide politics; not directly addressed.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Article 152 and the revolution's stance oppose Israel; Jewish Iranians are recognized as a minority but not the state.

revive-national-language.rationale: Article 15 sets Persian as official language; no revival issue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Constitution mentions workers' shares and shora councils; split on democratic company control.

school-vouchers.rationale: Constitution (Art. 30) provides free public education; vouchers not favored.

economic-freedom.rationale: Constitution protects lawful private enterprise but political freedom is not tied to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The theory stresses guardianship of pious jurists and moral rulers alongside law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Article 152 affirms independence and rejection of domination for every people.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religious democracy rests on faith-based law; the secular view criticizes it for putting scripture above reason.

class-collaboration.rationale: The constitution aims at justice and harmony between workers and employers and rejects class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The constitution aims to preserve cultural and Islamic heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Article 152 and 154 oppose domination by hegemonic powers and support oppressed peoples.

workers-nation.rationale: Constitution promotes Islamic ummah unity, not a national-only workers' movement.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 20 grants equality only as in conformity with Islamic criteria, which assigns distinct family roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest is forbidden under sharia, which Article 4 requires laws to follow; banking is interest-free in law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 19 gives all people equal rights regardless of ethnic group or race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is held to serve Islamic justice rather than a class.

national-mission.rationale: The revolution is framed as a model for Muslims; the constitution commits to exporting no force but supports oppressed peoples.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Adherents deny that Islamic law structurally disadvantages women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Reformers accuse elites; officials deny; split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The constitution assigns the state wide duties in economy, welfare, culture and religion.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Islamic universalism and Article 19 reject racial hierarchy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 2 affirms human dignity and Article 14 respect for non-Muslims, though legal rights vary by religion and gender.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Iranian state opposes Israel as a colonial project; stated in revolutionary foreign policy.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Article 13 lets recognized minorities follow their own personal-status law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion away from Islam is restricted in Islamic law and proselytizing by non-Muslims is limited.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Islamic practice permits and regulates halal slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Islamic education is part of the state curriculum under the constitution.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Article 6 requires public affairs be run by public opinion expressed through elections and referenda; Art. 56 gives people their destiny.

population-transfer.rationale: Article 14 requires treating non-Muslims with justice and respect; forced removal is not endorsed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Islamic law permits force in defense of faith and state and in penal enforcement; the absolutist non-aggression principle is not held.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cooperation and justice are emphasized over struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Article 26 allows parties only if they do not violate Islamic and Republic principles.

separated-powers.rationale: Article 57 divides power among legislature, executive and judiciary and states they are independent.

vanguard-party.rationale: The theory has no vanguard party; rule is by elections and jurist oversight.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Article 3 and 43 commit the state to ending deprivation and helping the deprived.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Islamic justice blames unjust structures over population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices are filled by elections and appointments under Articles 62, 107 and 115.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitution allows martial law (Art. 79) under limits; contested.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Leader commands the armed forces under Article 110, not a party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Art. 152 stresses independence; pooling sovereignty with Western blocs is rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Article 110 makes the Leader commander-in-chief with power to appoint key officials.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Adherents defend their own state in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Art. 24 limits publications harmful to Islam; censorship of art violating morals is practiced.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The constitution limits the president to two consecutive terms (Art. 114).

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Article 152 and 146 forbid foreign bases and favor non-alignment.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Article 31 right to housing; no ban on renting is advocated.

people-in-arms.rationale: Article 151 calls for military readiness, with a regular army and Basij volunteers; not replaced.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Religious democrats hold Islamic values superior or privileged over others.

death-penalty.rationale: Islamic penal law prescribes execution for grave crimes; adherents support it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Education is to follow Islamic criteria; gender equality education is accepted only as in Islamic terms.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Prohibited under Islamic criteria; Art. 24 restricts what is harmful to Islam.

minority-language-support.rationale: Article 15 permits regional and tribal languages in press, media and schools.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Article 13 lets recognized religious minorities act according to their own rites and personal law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The theory prefers conformity to religious norms.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Article 43 aims at economic independence and ending foreign domination.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1979 constitution itself was drafted and ratified by an elected Assembly of Experts and referendum.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The state asserts independence and self-reliance in defense.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Iran's president is directly elected (Art. 114) but the Leader is chosen by the Assembly of Experts.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banking is state-owned in Article 44, so independence from elected government is not favored.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 47 respects lawful ownership while Article 44 and 49 subordinate it to Islamic justice and public welfare.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religious institutions are strengthened, with jurists overseeing state; curbing clergy is rejected.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Leader is supposed to be above factions but it is contested.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The constitution declares territorial integrity inviolable and the army guards it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Leader is a jurist, not a divine descendant; the theory excludes divine descent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Article 107 makes the Leader equal before the law and the constitution binds all officials.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The system mixes elected bodies and unelected jurists, but not framed that way.

leader-cult.rationale: Revolutionary leadership is honored but formal cults of personality are criticized by adherents.

land-redistribution.rationale: Article 49 mandates confiscation of illicit wealth, but not general land redistribution.

women-must-cover.rationale: Hijab is legally required in Iran under Islamic criteria.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Art. 13 grants recognized minorities institutions, but not for all peoples; split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The theory holds faith and divine will central rather than materialism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The theory limits majority choice by religious law; Guardian Council vetoes bills it finds non-compliant.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equality only in conformity with Islamic criteria; parity quotas not favored.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-sufficiency aims exist but a closed bloc is not claimed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Article 3 and 19 abolish privilege; Article 107 equal before law.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Education is to be centered on Islamic and Iranian culture.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-colonial stance rejects rule by advanced societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Art. 30 and 3 emphasise cultural and national values in schooling.

delink-world-market.rationale: Self-reliance valued but full delinking not endorsed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article 19 equal rights, and Islamic criteria restrict freedom of business conduct.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution entrenches rights, with Guardian Council review.

elective-rulers.rationale: Presidency and Assembly of Experts are elected under Articles 62 and 107.

minority-veto.rationale: Decisions by majority under the constitution; no individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Article 5 and 110 condition the Leader's legitimacy on justice and the law; removal is possible when unqualified.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament legislates but is subordinate to Guardian Council and Leader.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Islamic tradition requires humane treatment of animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Islamic law permits use for food and research with humane handling.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Islamic charity and justice oblige the wealthy to help the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Religious democracy is a form of engaged political religion.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Independence and self-sufficiency are constitutional goals (Art. 43).

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Article 19 gives equal rights to all peoples; rule by descent group not supported.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Muslim democrats argue for forms rooted in Islamic rather than Western liberal values, and reject imported Western institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Article 144 gives the army an ideological role in guarding the revolution, but not constitutional guardianship as such.

filial-duty.rationale: Respect for parents is a core Islamic duty and the family is fundamental under Article 10.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Islamic family law gives men and courts specific grounds; adherents resist fault-free divorce.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social insurance is a state duty under Article 29.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Article 47 respects private ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Article 52 requires the annual budget to be submitted to and passed by parliament.

single-official-language.rationale: Article 15 makes Persian official but allows regional languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Independence emphasis; Art. 81 bans foreign concessions in commerce and industry.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Article 43 and Islamic ethics oppose consumption excess and wastefulness.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Article 154 supports just struggles but bars interference; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Article 152 and 154 reject domination and interference in others' internal affairs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family strengthening is a constitutional aim (Art. 10); Iran has adopted pronatalist policies.

job-guarantee.rationale: Article 28 requires the government to create equal conditions for employment for everyone.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Obedience to Islamic law and legitimate authority is a religious duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Article 154 forbids interference in other nations' internal affairs, though it also supports oppressed peoples.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Article 14 conditions non-Muslim rights on not conspiring, but a minority-conspiracy thesis is not a position of the theory.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is a religious-legal institution central to the family under Islamic law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Article 24 and 175 give access to media and open public discourse, with limits.

informal-organisation.rationale: The theory works through parties, elections and institutions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Article 4 and independence emphasis place Islamic constitution above external law.

religious-nation.rationale: Religious democracy builds a state on a preferred religion; Article 12 makes Islam official.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Article 152 rejects any form of foreign domination and hegemony.

defeat-communism.rationale: Article 152 non-alignment toward both blocs; not a stated mission.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religious democracy rests on religion as a true guide to politics.

socialized-care.rationale: The family is the fundamental unit and care is a family function under Article 10.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Article 44 gives cooperatives a sector; small communities not a theory theme.

majority-settlement.rationale: Article 19 and 14 require equal rights and justice; engineered settlement is not endorsed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Iranian official doctrine claims an Islamic third way and rejects both East and West.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a doctrine of religious democracy; some officials deny it, but adherents as a group do not define it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Same-sex relations are a criminal offence under Islamic law which grounds legislation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The theory makes people the basis of legitimacy with a role in government, though party freedom has limits.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Islamic penal law punishes blasphemy; Article 24 limits expression harmful to Islam.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Classical Islamic law makes defense of a Muslim land an obligation on all; mainstream view, not only Salafi-jihadist.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Articles 6, 7 and 100 provide for elections, referenda and local councils for people's participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not a framework of religious democracy.

assisted-dying.rationale: Islamic law holds life sacred and forbids suicide and assisting it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Muslim democrats argue Islam is compatible with democracy.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Article 56 says absolute sovereignty belongs to God, with the people exercising a God-given right to their destiny.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Hijab is required in state institutions in Iran; adherents reject bans on religious dress.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Articles 143 and 144 require the army to defend independence and territorial integrity.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Article 152 pursues non-alignment toward hegemonic superpowers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Leader is selected by the Assembly of Experts for qualifications, not by descent.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Interest-free banking under sharia; mutual credit is compatible.

property-franchise.rationale: Article 62 and 6 give universal elections by secret ballot.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claims are not part of the theory, and Islamic framing of nature as trust under God differs from that link.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Article 4 and the Guardian Council framework require known laws and Article 36 requires courts to apply laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Article 19 equality of all peoples regardless of race; Article 62 universal vote.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Islamic law forbids Muslim women marrying non-Muslim men, applied in Iranian law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Article 14 requires just treatment of non-Muslims.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Article 49 confiscation of illicit wealth; Islamic justice opposes concentrations.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Same-sex conduct is criminal under Islamic law.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Article 2 and 12 make belief in God and Islam the foundation.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The state enforces Islamic criminal law through police and courts.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Article 64 reserves seats for recognized minorities but executive power is not shared.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Religious charity is prized but the constitution also commits the state to social security.

term-limits.rationale: Article 114 limits the president to two consecutive terms.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not part of the theory; representative elections used.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Iranian model reserves top religious posts for male jurists; reformist strands dissent.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Islamic family law gives the husband headship; Article 20 equality only under Islamic criteria.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Basij youth organisation exists but not a stated doctrine of the theory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Article 146 forbids establishing any foreign military base in Iran.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Article 46 protects income from work and Article 47 legitimate ownership; split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Islamic law allows self-defense and defense of others.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Islamic criteria assume fixed sexes; not a theory position.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Martyrdom is honoured; the constitution protects the families of martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Religious democracy rests on faith guiding politics.

god-not-male.rationale: Traditional Islamic theology does not describe God in gendered terms but this feminist position is not adopted.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Scripture and Islamic criteria are the standard, not judged by outside tests.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Article 44 puts basic services and utilities in the state sector.

second-chamber.rationale: The Guardian Council functions as a check but parliament is unicameral (Art. 62); the 1989 abolition of the Senate.

municipal-property.rationale: Article 44 and 47 recognise state, cooperative and private ownership, not community-owned production as the basis.

family-wage.rationale: Article 43 requires meeting basic needs and Article 10 family strengthening.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Religious democracy is premised on a religion's view of human nature and spiritual goals for politics.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Article 19 equal rights regardless of race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Articles 143 and 152 stress defense and no domination.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Religion defines the community in the theory, with Persian being one official language among many.

communal-electorates.rationale: Article 64 reserves seats for minorities but they are chosen by general votes.

free-public-college.rationale: Article 30 provides free education up to secondary and expansion of higher education.

future-generations.rationale: Article 50 makes environmental protection a duty for present and future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Islamic framing stresses distinct complementary roles.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Article 144-151 vest military power in state forces, though Basij paramilitary exist.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Opposition to domination by hegemonic powers favors restructuring.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The revolution did replace the state but the theory preserves institutions.

sacred-nation.rationale: The sacred community is the Islamic ummah, not the nation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Article 2 affirms the dignity of man and God's creation of a shared human nature.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Islam is held to be the final truth; pluralist unity of all religions is not the official position.

farm-price-support.rationale: State support for agriculture is part of the economic plan.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Islamic inheritance law gives women half shares in many cases; Article 20 equal protection only under Islamic criteria.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Law is made by parliament and jurists.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Islamic penal law fixes penalties for hudud crimes.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Article 12 gives Twelver Jafari Islam legal precedence as official religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Religious democrats require democracy to include religious values, not just fair elections.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Iranian constitution gives women equal participation in elections and public life, though with equal rights stated as in conformity with Islamic criteria.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Adherents of the Iranian-Islamic formulation hold that religion protects women's dignity; the constitution describes the family and women's role in Islamic terms.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The constitution grounds law in the Quran as divine revelation, though jurists interpret it by ijtihad rather than plain literal reading, and reformists such as Soroush treat interpretation as fallible.

indirect-election.rationale: The constitution provides direct popular election of the president and parliament, and the theory centres on the people's vote.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution makes Twelver Ja'fari Islam the official religion, with other recognised faiths given only limited protection.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The constitution provides for a unitary state with local languages and provincial councils but no ethnic territorial autonomy.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The constitution requires trial in a competent court for punishment and bars arbitrary detention, so killing without trial contradicts the system's own legal framework.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The constitution guarantees universal social security yet also stresses aid to the needy, so adherents are not clearly either way.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Khamenei's theory ties people and leader through elections and institutions rather than bypassing them, and the constitution permits parties within Islamic limits.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The constitution makes Twelver Ja'fari Shi'ism the official religion and bases the state on it, so politics is organised along a religious line.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Khamenei's theory presents an Islamic-Iranian model of progress that pursues science and modernity while grounded in religious values.

national-resource-control.rationale: The constitution bars foreign concessions and national resources are state-held, reflecting the independence principle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Article 4 makes any law contrary to Islamic criteria void, which parallels the idea that a law violating a higher standard does not bind.

multipolar-world.rationale: The constitution's foreign policy rejects domination by any power, 'neither East nor West', and Khamenei's theory opposes a unipolar order.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: A communist-party-led socialist system is foreign to the theory, which is clerical-Islamic, though it allows a mixed economy.

missingStatements.text: Laws passed by an elected parliament should be reviewed by a council of religious jurists and rejected if they conflict with religious law.
missingStatements.rationale: The Guardian Council vetoes bills it finds incompatible with sharia (Article 4 and the council's role).

missingStatements.text: Citizens should choose their rulers by election, within limits set by religious law.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 6 requires public affairs be run through elections while Article 4 subordinates all laws to Islamic criteria; the theory centers on this combination.

missingStatements.text: Women and men should have equal rights only to the extent the rights are consistent with religious law.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 20 grants equal rights to men and women only in conformity with Islamic criteria.

notes: Strands differ: Soroush-style reformers treat sharia as fallible and reject punishing disbelief, while the official Iranian model and Maududi's theo-democracy give religious law and jurists binding authority. Answers follow the official model; where sources do not address a statement the answer is a low-confidence inference.
